title: Improved protocol for spawning and immunostaining embryos and juvenile stages of the ctenophore _Mnemiopsis leidyi_
protocol: Collect adult _Mnemiopsis leidyi_ using beakers from floating docks in the Intercostal Waterway around Marineland, Florida or Eel Pond in Woods Hole, Massachusetts.
Transfer adults into a 5-gallon plastic bucket filled with natural 1 µm UV-filtered fresh seawater (1x UV-FSW).
Keep the bucket inside the lab at room temperature under constant light for at least two consecutive nights before spawning.
Place a 20-Watt LED Floodlight or similar lighting source at the top of the bucket to provide continuous light exposure.
Take 1-2 adult M. leidyi from the bucket.
Place the adults into a new container with fresh 1 µm UV-FSW.
Transfer the animals using glass or plastic beakers, avoiding direct contact.
Place the bowls containing the animals in complete darkness.
Check the bowls after 1-2 hours for early spawning.
If gametes are detected, transfer the animals to a clean bowl with fresh 1x FSW.
Keep animals in darkness during spawning.
After 3 hours, collect sperm and eggs once sperm release is observed.
Collect fertilized eggs with a pipette after egg release.
Transfer collected fertilized eggs to a dish of freshly filtered seawater.
Return adults to a bucket of fresh seawater.
Collect the fertilized eggs using a pipette when they sink to the bottom of the dish.
Transfer the fertilized eggs into a dish containing freshly filtered seawater to avoid contamination.
Let the embryos develop until the desired stage.
Transfer embryos into a 35 mm plastic petri dish with ice-cold fixative using a mouth or micropipette.
Incubate embryos in the fixative for 1.5 to 2 hours on a rocking platform at room temperature with the lid on.
Transfer fixed embryos to a new petri dish and rinse them twice (5 minutes each) with 1x FSW on a rocking platform at room temperature.
Replace 1x FSW with PBT.
Dechorionate fixed embryos using sharp Dumont #5 forceps.
Rinse fixed embryos at least five times in PBT for at least 3 hours on a rocking platform at room temperature.
Replace PBT with 5% NGS for 1-2 hours at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Store fixed embryos overnight in 5% NGS at 4°C if needed.
Dilute primary antibodies to the desired concentration in ice-cold 5% NGS on ice.
Remove blocking solution \(5% NGS).
Replace it with the prepared primary antibody solution.
Incubate overnight on a rocker at 4°C.
Rinse fixed embryos five times in PBT for a total period of 3 hours on a rocking platform at room temperature.
Wash fixed embryos twice with PBT for at least an hour each on a rocking platform at room temperature after secondary antibody incubation.
Incubate samples for 1.5 hours with Phalloidin diluted 1:200 in PBT on a rocking platform at room temperature.
Wash the samples once with PBT.
Incubate samples with DAPI at 0.1 µg/µl in PBT for 1 hour on a rocking platform at room temperature.
Rinse Samples in PBT.
Store Samples at 4°C.
Embed live ctenophore specimens in pre-warmed low melt agar at 1.2% in 1x FSW.
Pipette specimens into a petri dish or microscope slide with minimum volume of water.
(Optional) Add Sodium Azide to 1x FSW containing animals for relaxation and tentacle extension, using final concentrations from 10 mM (0.065%) to 25 mM (0.1625%).
Carefully add liquid agar in a ratio of approximately 10:1 (agar:1x FSW/animals volume) to the specimens.
Mix well and gently until sea water is fully dissolved and specimens are fully embedded into the agar.
Pipette some agar to the side of the water containing the specimens.
Pipette up the agar with the specimens and mix solutions by gently pipetting up and down two to three times.
(Optional) Put a coverslip with clay corners over the samples and press down until desired thickness.
Quickly cool the slide on ice until the agar is solidified and animals stop moving their ctenes.
Pour 1-3 ml of ice-cold fixative over the agar containing the specimens in a 35 mm plastic petri dish.
Incubate in the fixative for 1.5 to 2 hours on a rocking platform at room temperature.
Discard the fixative and rinse twice with 1x FSW on a rocking platform at room temperature.
Replace 1x FSW with PBT.
Cut agar into cubes using a clean scalpel or razor blade, ensuring each cube contains an intact sample embedded inside.
Transfer the cubes of agar to a new 2 mL tube.
Transfer individual stained samples in PBT into a microscope slide.
Put a coverslip with clay “feet” on the corners over the samples and press down on the corners until desired thickness.
Add the mounting media to one side of the coverslip.
At the other side of the coverslip put an absorptive tissue to create a directional flow that will replace the PBT and embed the stained samples with the desired mounting media.
Replace PBT with TDE.
Replace PBT with PBS.
Dehydrate samples with isopropanol using the gradient 50%, 75%, 90%, and 100%.
Replace isopropanol with MMM.
